title: Surge mitigation & GPU safety stock by region (hosted API)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a proposed operational approach for hosted API surge mitigation by region (tokens/sec and QPS) and the GPU safety-stock we should carry to meet headroom targets.

Scope:
- Hosted API (public tenants) only — Dedicated and Private are out of scope here.
- Time horizon: next 6–9 months (2026 Q2–Q3 ramp planning).
- Targets: p95 latency <= 350ms for text-gen small models; prioritize availability over nominal cost during surges.

Summary of approach (short):
1) Define regional peak-to-average multipliers from historical 2025–early-2026 traces.
2) Convert peak tokens/sec to baseline GPU demand using per-GPU token throughput profiles per model family.
3) Add three layers of buffer: operating headroom (20%), hot-burst lane (10% oversub of spare GPUs), and safety-stock (N GPUs by region) to cover AZ outages and bursty telemetries.
4) Maintain a thin global overflow lane (cross-region) that can take lightweight requests when local region is saturated.

Assumptions (conservative unless noted):
- Typical model mix at peak: 40% chat-large, 30% chat-medium, 20% text-gen-small, 10% embeddings/rerank.
- GPU throughput (tokens/sec) at 80% util target:
  - A100-80GB (fp16 / q8*): 28k tokens/sec (chat-large profile)
  - H100-80GB (fp16 / q8*): 45k tokens/sec (chat-large profile)
  - A10G: 9k tokens/sec (text-gen-small)
- KV cache hit rate baseline for chat = 18% at peak; effective tokens/sec demand reduced accordingly when cache applies.
- Latency SLO prioritized; therefore we size to 80% steady util (not >85% sustained).

Regional projection table (working numbers):
Columns: REGION | avg_tokens/s | historical-peak-mult | projected-peak-tokens/s | headroom % | provisioned-gpus (baseline) | hot-burst-reserve-gpus | safety-stock-gpus
us-west-1 | 420k | 2.1 | 882k | 30% | 30 H100 equiv | 4 | 3
us-east-1 | 520k | 2.4 | 1,248k | 30% | 42 H100 equiv | 6 | 4
eu-west-1 | 210k | 2.0 | 420k | 35% | 12 H100 equiv | 2 | 2
ap-southeast-1 | 95k | 2.8 | 266k | 40% | 6 H100 equiv | 1 | 1

Notes on calc method:
- projected-peak-tokens/s = avg_tokens/s * historical-peak-mult
- provisioned-gpus (baseline) = ceil(projected-peak-tokens/s / (H100_throughput * (1 - headroom%))) expressed in H100-equivalent (we use H100 as standard).
- hot-burst-reserve expressed as small integer GPUs that are kept idling or put into fast-warm pool.
- safety-stock for AZ failure: minimum 2 GPUs or 10% of baseline (whichever is larger), tuned by region criticality.

Example calculation (us-east-1):
- avg = 520,000 tps, multiplier = 2.4 -> peak = 1,248,000 tps.
- headroom = 30% -> usable per H100 = 45k * (1 - 0.30) = 31,500 tps.
- baseline GPUs = ceil(1,248,000 / 31,500) = 40 GPUs -> round up to 42 for placement/frag.

Oversubscription and cost controls:
- During steady-state (non-peak hours) we can oversubscribe to 1.6x for cheaper SKUs (A10G/A100 mix) but we must guarantee fast scale-up windows (<=5m) to reach H100-backed capacity for peaks.
- Use model-family routing: route embeddings and rerank (low-latency cheap paths) to A10 pool to preserve H100 for chat workloads.

Operational playbooks / automation we need:
- Automated regional scale-up policy triggered by sustained p90 tokens/s > 75% of baseline for 3m.
- Canary cold-to-warm transition for hot-burst lane: pre-warm images and model weights kept on local NVMe to reduce startup to <90s.
- Cross-region failover policy: lightweight requests (embeddings, small text-gen) eligible for global overflow; chat-large not eligible unless model-family variant exists in target region.

Open questions & TODOs (for triage):
- Verification: validate assumed H100 throughput per model at target seq lengths; schedule microbench runs (PR: #417) on mixed sequences (8–256).
- Policy: decide exact percent for headroom per region (EU currently conservative at 35% — can we reduce to 30% if we accept 2x hot-burst)?
- Economics: produce monthly cost delta between current fleet and proposed baseline+hot-burst+safety-stock (Finance to run).
- SLA language: define customer-facing message for transient throttling during global surges.

Quick risk register (short):
- AZ GPU hardware failure: mitigated by safety-stock + cross-AZ placement; residual risk: short-term tail latency bursts.
- Model change regressions increasing tokens/sec per unit request: mitigate with model-level quotas and automatic scale experiments.
- Cold-starts for hot-burst: mitigate with fast-warm lane; residual: slight increase in p95 during immediate surge.

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- Maya (owner) -> run H100 microbench matrix for chat-large/chat-medium/text-gen-small by 2026-03-24 (ENGINF-3421).
- Diego -> draft AutoScale runbook + Terraform templates for hot-burst pools by 2026-03-17.
- Priya -> cost delta spreadsheet and monthly burn model by 2026-03-22 (share in Finance review).
- Owen -> implement cross-region overflow routing prototype (canary) by 2026-04-01.

Appendix: quick formulas
- GPUs_needed = ceil(peak_tokens_per_sec / (per_gpu_tokens_per_sec * (1 - headroom_fraction)))
- safety_stock = max(ceil(baseline_gpus * 0.10), 2)
- hot_burst_count ~ ceil(baseline_gpus * 0.10) (min 1)

Contact / provenance:
- Drafted by Maya Chen (eng-infrastructure).
- This is a working doc: expect numbers to change after microbench runs and finance pass.
- Slack: #infra-capacity (thread pinned: 2026-02-02).
